significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that the measurable ordering between the model's "commitment point" and the fact-determining token predicts later belief-versus-fact errors, varies with prior strength, and causally contributes to those errors when commitment is advanced or delayed; this is primarily a form-(iii) predictive coupling plus a form-(ii) causal mechanism. The phenomenon would constrain expected error rates for late-decidable and garden-path propositions, while the mechanism would explain those errors as premature stabilization rather than merely showing a decodable truth axis—the kind of static representation characterized by Marks and Tegmark's COLM 2024 work, "The Geometry of Truth." Verified-false and verified-true are distinguishable: a negative result would rule against timing of truth-direction stabilization as a general explanation or predictor of belief–fact confusion, although failure of only the proposed direction would not rule out all forms of commitment. In the topic-substitution check, generic research on LLM beliefs would not warrant this score; the specific commitment/disambiguation ordering and its claimed predictive and causal consequences make it sharper than the topic-median hypothesis.

reach.justification: The principal handle is the claim's "commitment-lead metric (tokens between commitment and disambiguation)," supplemented by the intervention of "causally delaying commitment" through attenuation of the truth direction. Commitment-lead is mainly post hoc because its definition depends on subsequent stabilization to the final judgment and a known disambiguation position; the intervention likewise needs knowledge of where disambiguation occurs, limiting immediate deployment as a general-purpose gate. After per-model re-extraction, however, the asserted relation—that positive commitment-lead predicts errors better than final-token confidence and scales with prior or garden-path strength—would predict what should be found across the stated class of open-weight model families, rather than supplying only a search procedure. The likely downstream users are interpretability and model-auditing researchers rather than general deployers, and the topic-substitution check does not preserve the score: its reach comes specifically from the transferable metric–error relation and intervention, not from LLM-belief research in general.
